A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LRM/LPO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, with retained content identifiable across reformatting, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original LRM/LPO evaluations, training-efficiency measurements, ablations, and a 200-prompt human evaluation in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds experiments involving step-wise GRPO, SD3-medium, HPDv2 training, and additional controls.

M1.justification: The original LRM architecture, MPCF, and LPO procedure are retained, but Appendix B introduces substantial extensions: an LRM-based step-wise GRPO optimizer and an SD3 adaptation using MMDiT features, frozen text encoders, and stochastic flow-matching sampling. These change the available procedures rather than merely explaining the existing method.

E1.justification: V3 adds LRM/LPO training on HPDv2 and automatic evaluation on held-out HPDv2 prompts. V2 used HPSv2 benchmark prompts in its human study but trained LRM/LPO on Pick-a-Pic. This extends data coverage within the existing text-to-image preference tasks; GenEval, T2I-CompBench++, and DPG-Bench were already present.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add SePPO for SD1.5 and the comparator labeled InterComp for SDXL, corresponding to the IterComp reference. Appendix B also compares LPO against the new step-wise GRPO variant. Existing DDPO, D3PO, Diffusion-DPO, MaPO, and SPO comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds 50-step GenEval evaluation, a single-A100 sampling-time protocol, and experimental settings for GRPO, SD3, HPDv2, and fixed-timestep controls. The original 20-step LPO evaluation and core training settings remain. Separately, v3 Table 2 labels DDPO's training data as Pick-a-Pic v2, conflicting with Appendix A's retained v1 description, so that setting cannot be resolved.

E4.justification: Appendix C expands the existing no-MPCF ablation into a direct comparison with SPO, adds SPO's reported high-noise failures alongside LPO, and introduces a control supplying timestep zero throughout LPO sampling. These strengthen tests of filtering dependence, high-noise compatibility, and timestep sensitivity. The original VFE, filtering, timestep-range, threshold, and regularization ablations remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A newly states that evaluations use the same random seed. This adds seed-control information without establishing additional runs. Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the five-evaluator human-study protocol is unchanged.

E6.justification: V3 adds comparator scores, 50-step GenEval results, GRPO and SD3 results, HPDv2 results, and timing/control measurements. For example, Table 12 newly reports GRPO GenEval 45.88 versus LPO 48.39, with reported training times of 64 versus 8 A100 hours. The original 20-step LPO GenEval scores of 48.39 for SD1.5 and 59.27 for SDXL, and the human-study outcomes, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds normalized advantage definitions and a clipped GRPO objective, followed by a derivation of stochastic flow-matching updates in Equations 14–15. These are localized mathematical additions. The original diffusion equations, preference losses, filtering assumptions, and threshold formulas are otherwise retained despite notation and numbering changes.

C1.justification: The central claims about latent reward modeling, preference alignment, and 2.5–28-fold training speedups remain. The introduction additionally claims applicability to step-wise GRPO and DiT-based SD3, extending the demonstrated scope beyond the original U-Net/LPO experiments.

C2.justification: V3 removes the stated U-Net/DDPM-only applicability limitation following the SD3 experiment. It also softens v2's characterization of unfiltered training as ineffective by emphasizing that LPO without MPCF still exceeds SPO in general preference and alignment. New discussion acknowledges GRPO's performance/compute tradeoff; the existing latent-space compatibility and broader-impact qualifications remain.

D1.justification: V3 explains its shared evaluation pipeline, official-checkpoint use without retraining, and discrepancies with SPO's published scores. Appendix B supplies GRPO hyperparameters, SD3 feature-layer and encoder-freezing choices, and HPDv2 sampling instructions. The original U-Net training hyperparameters, hardware disclosure, and code/model access statement are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds DeepSeekMath as the GRPO foundation and expands related work with newer multimodal reward models, SePPO, IterComp, ranked preference optimization, and training-free alignment. The explicit LLaVA citation is removed. These broaden the existing discussion while retaining the central novelty claim of using diffusion models themselves for reward modeling.

P1.justification: V3 refines the abstract, introduction, and experimental explanations, renames Background and Methodology, consolidates training descriptions, and adds an author. The appendices separate exploration from ablation experiments and relocate the impact statement to Appendix E. The main section sequence and much of the method exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column layout and substantially restructures its displays. The workflow diagram becomes four panels explicitly contrasting SPO and LPO sampling; Table 2 combines preference and GenEval summaries, while full GenEval breakdowns move to Appendix Tables 25–26. Numerous experimental tables are added, whereas the qualitative appendix images are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens validation of the central approach. The SD3 experiment tests beyond v2's explicitly stated U-Net/DDPM limitation, while the matched-data and fixed-timestep controls better establish what LRM/LPO contributes. Broader comparisons and clearer evaluation disclosure further improve the evidence. New reporting inconsistencies, including DDPO's conflicting dataset labels and InterComp's 59.65 versus 59.64 GenEval entries in Tables 2 and 26, limit precision but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
